atoms.b: Plants ((++cannot can)) move from place to place.
Once a seed has ((++germinated generated)) and grown its first root, the plant will grow in the same spot for the rest of its life.
When plants produce seeds, the seeds must be ((++dispersed kept_close)), or scattered away from the plant, in order to give new plants room to grow.
Some seeds are collected, buried and forgotten by ((++animals bees)).
Others are caught in ((++fur nets)) and eventually fall off in new places.
Many animals also eat ((++fruits cake)). The seeds of fruits are not digested and are spread through the animals’ ((++droppings skeleton)) later.

atoms.b: Some other seeds are dispersed by the ((++wind sun)).
These seeds have adapted to be ((++light heavy)) and fly well. Once they’re ripe and ready, they ((++let_go_of cling_to)) the plant and are carried away by the breeze.

atoms.b: Some plants, like ((++peas potatoes)), can disperse their seeds themselves. Pea pods dry out and ((++burst_open shrivel_up)), releasing seeds in all directions.

text: Burdock seeds have lots of small hooks. They can easily get caught in fur or clothing and be dispersed.

feedback.correct: The tumbling part of tumbleweed is detached from its roots. Wind pushes the tumbleweed around, dispersing its seeds. Once the seeds land on fertile soil, new tumbleweed plants can grow.

atoms.a: What happens after the seeds are dispersed?

b.sound: If the seeds land on fertile soil after they’ve been dispersed, roots start to form and a new plant can grow.
